transactions.citation: p1850: 'On 29 October 2024, MIT acquired a freehold property in Tokyo from Nagayama Tokutei Mokuteki Kaisha at a purchase consideration of JPY14.5 billion... The agreed property value represented approximately 3.3% discount to JLL Morii Valuation & Advisory K.K.'s independent valuation of JPY15.0 billion.'; footnote 4 (p1858): 'MIT has an effective economic interest of 98.47% in the property while the remaining 1.53% is held by its Sponsor, MIPL.'; footnote 5 (p1860): 'JLL Morii Valuation & Advisory K.K. valued the property based on the cost approach and income capitalisation approach methods and concluded a market value of JPY15.0 billion as at 31 July 2024.'
transactions.notes: No gain/loss concept applies to an acquisition per SPEC, so the five divestment fields are left null even though the AR explicitly discloses a DISCOUNT-to-valuation percentage for this deal (purchase consideration JPY14.5bn vs JLL Morii independent valuation JPY15.0bn as at 31 Jul 2024 = approximately 3.3% discount, disclosed verbatim in the Manager's narrative, cross-checked: (14.5-15.0)/15.0*100 = -3.33%, rounds to the disclosed 3.3%). purchase_price recorded on the JPY-denominated, effective-98.47%-interest basis as disclosed (remaining 1.53% held by Sponsor MIPL). A separate SGD-denominated audited figure exists in the Portfolio Statement -- acquisition cash outflow S$131,341k (Statement of Cash Flows) vs 31 Mar 2025 portfolio valuation S$135,272k -- which corroborates the discount at a ~-2.9% level (different currency conversion date and a fair-value date 8 months later than the JPY figures above), but that SGD acquisition-cost figure is not used here to avoid mixing an FX-converted cash-outflow number against the JPY-denominated purchase consideration disclosed for the deal itself.
